name: Kale
summary: Kale is a leafy cruciferous vegetable with curly or flat dark leaves. This page lists what people say kale does and what writers in ancient Rome believed about curly cabbage; each claim can be checked against the research when you choose.
inIt: A 2019 review calls kale a cruciferous vegetable with leaves along the stem, popular as a 'superfood', and says it is unclear whether that label rests on scientific evidence rather than other factors.
Like other cruciferous vegetables it is rich in glucosinolates and the compounds they break down into (2007 review).

The UK food table (CoFID) measures raw curly kale at 33 kcal, 1.3 g of sugars, 450 mg of potassium, 130 mg of calcium, 525 µg of vitamin A (retinol equivalents), 623 µg of vitamin K1, 120 µg of folate and 110 mg of vitamin C per 100 g; fibre is not measured for the raw leaf. It does not measure glucosinolates or other plant compounds.

lore.who: Ancient Greece (Greek physicians quoted by Pliny the Elder, about 77 AD)
lore.belief: Pliny reports that the most ancient Greek writers described three kinds of cabbage, and that the curly kind, named 'selinoides' because its leaf resembles parsley, is good for the stomach and moderately loosens the bowels.
lore.note: This is the curly cabbage of the ancient writers, the closest ancient plant to modern curly kale, though it is not certain to be the same plant.

sources.title: Pliny the Elder, Natural History 20.33 (the cabbage and Cato's remedies), Bostock and Riley translation, 1855
sources.author: Pliny the Elder

lore.who: Ancient Rome (Cato the Elder, as reported by Pliny the Elder, about 77 AD)
lore.belief: Cato esteemed the curly cabbage most highly of all and said that cabbage taken raw in the morning with oxymel, coriander, rue, mint and silphium root is good for headache, dim or dazzled sight, the spleen, the stomach and the chest.
lore.note: The translators' footnote says that most of the stated virtues of cabbage are quite untrue. As above, the curly cabbage is only the closest ancient match to kale.

tableFoods.label: 1 handful of raw curly kale (about 40 g)

processing: Boiling curly kale in unsalted water lowers the vitamin C in the UK food table from 110 mg to 25 mg per 100 g and the folate from 120 µg to 97 µg.

claims.claim: Kale has more calcium than milk and builds strong bones
claims.label: Kale calcium and bones

whoShouldBeCareful.with: Warfarin and other vitamin K blockers
whoShouldBeCareful.note: Kale is one of the richest vegetable sources of vitamin K1: 623 µg per 100 g raw in the UK food table. A 2016 systematic review of 11 studies (2 diet trials, 9 observational) found conflicting evidence on whether dietary vitamin K changes the blood-thinning effect, and said an effect may show only with high intakes (above 150 µg a day). Talk to your doctor or anticoagulation clinic about green vegetables if you take a vitamin K blocker such as warfarin.

whoShouldBeCareful.with: Thyroid conditions or low iodine intake
whoShouldBeCareful.note: A 2016 review found that some Russian kale (Brassica napus) holds enough goitrin to potentially lower the thyroid's iodine uptake, while kale of Brassica oleracea (the usual curly kale) holds under 10 µmol per 100 g, which it called minimal risk. If you have a thyroid condition, talk to your doctor.

unknowns: Whether kale is better for health than other vegetables: the 2019 review says this is unclear.
How much vitamin K1 there is in a cooked portion: the UK food table has no vitamin K1 value for boiled curly kale.
How much of the plant compounds that the food table does not measure survive cooking.
